column1: # Game profile of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (Switch, update 1.1.404 = v393216, the Anniversary Edition build)
# Bethesda's Creation Engine on SDK 14.3.0 (NVN, Havok); started from the provisional profile scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py wrote from its survey (dm/games/profile_guess.py)
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 in its first seconds: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# after its first frame the render thread waits for a timestamp report's counter field to read 0, as on the GPU; the host writes the time there unless render_cond is on,
# and the game presented one black frame and no more (seedds/nxnative PR #444 found the same wait on 1.0.12, main+0xb5e808)
# The NPDM declares 8 MB of system resource and main never sets a heap: the game's heaps are address regions it maps itself, four from main+0xacf43c (2 GB, 2 GB, 0.59 GB, 1 GB)
# and more after them, reaching alias +6.92 GB in its first 15 s, past the 4.375 GB an iPhone's 5 GB block holds. The Mac and Android give every game a Switch's 64 GB alias region
# whatever this says (hle_svc.c mem_init_once), so the profile names that much, as Unreal's bring-up profiles do; an iPhone would need the heap ceilings cut, as seedds/nxnative
# PR #444 does for 1.0.12 (Default and GPU heaps 2 → 1.5 GB, the small-block pool 1 GB → 256 MB)
# the NPDM declares 8 MB of system resource
# 23,080 shaders in Data/Skyrim - Shaders.bsa (shadersfx/shaders011.fxp) and 53 in main, NVN records each (shader_split.py fxp_shaders, bsa.py)
